chi_sono.titolo: From London, with a passion for *sharing* dance.
paragrafi: I'm Annagiulia Loffi and I have been dancing since I was a child in Parma. I'm currently studying at the Royal Academy of Dance in London, one of the world's leading institutions for training dance teachers, and will graduate in September 2027. I already hold RAD teaching certifications.

Alongside classical technique I practise contemporary dance: two languages that enrich each other. In my classes the precision of the method goes hand in hand with musicality, expression and the simple joy of moving, at any age.

metodo.titolo: The RAD method, an *international* standard, step by step.
paragrafi: Founded in London in 1920, the Royal Academy of Dance is one of the world's largest dance education organisations. Its syllabus guides students through a clear progression, built to develop technique, musicality and confidence safely and gradually.
Exams are optional, assessed by RAD examiners, and certify progress with an internationally recognised award.

prima_volta.testo: The questions parents and new students ask me most often. Can't find yours? Just write to me.

domande.risposta: Pre-ballet starts from age [4]; RAD Graded classes usually begin around [6–7]. There is no upper limit: there are classes for adult beginners too.

domande.domanda: What do I need for the first class?
domande.risposta: Comfortable, close-fitting clothes (a leotard, or a T-shirt and leggings), socks or ballet slippers if you have them, and hair tied back. I'll advise on uniform after your first class.

It is the classical ballet syllabus of the Royal Academy of Dance, founded in London in 1920, which trains teachers and runs exams worldwide. It progresses level by level, from first steps for young children to professional levels, building technique, musicality and expression gradually and safely.
No, they are optional. Students who wish to can prepare during the year: exams are assessed by a Royal Academy of Dance examiner and lead to an internationally recognised award.

domande.domanda: Ballet or contemporary: which to choose?
domande.risposta: For younger students I recommend starting with ballet, which builds the technical foundation, then adding contemporary to develop freedom and expression. Adults can start with either.
